_doc: Shared canonical ERC-20 metadata fixture for the ADR-005 Tier-2 dual-driver parity tests (VK3YDM-S6). Loaded by BOTH rust/crates/degenbot/tests/parity_erc20.rs (Rust consumer: build_erc20_metadata over a ConstructionIo whose fake Rpc RPC serves name()/symbol()/decimals()+non-empty get_code) AND tests/standalone_parity/test_erc20_dual_driver.py (Python consumer: PyBot.build_erc20_token over an offline alloy provider). The fixture holds the plain canonical metadata (no RPC cassette) - each side ABI-encodes the SAME name()/symbol()/decimals() from `fixture` into its provider double with no DB row (both NoDb and a DB-less offline provider resolve DB-first to None, then on-chain), then asserts the resolved (name, symbol, decimals) equals `expected`. A deliberately-wrong edit to THIS file fails BOTH sides mechanically (the shared-fixture contract, HRT356). Keeps `fixture.metadata == expected` by default so a one-sided edit drifts the RPC payload away from the asserted output and fails one side.

fixture.name: Wrapped Ether
fixture._note: The plain canonical metadata both sides ABI-encode into their provider doubles (a DB-miss -> full on-chain resolution).

expected.name: Wrapped Ether
expected._note: What BOTH consumers must resolve from the SAME plain fixture - proving the DB-first + on-chain resolution is lossless across the FFI seam.
